translation_notes: context shim: nanopub_shim.py puts the Nanopublication/nanopub-py@05022dc4bc checkout on sys.path (the package is not installed); one added import line, identical on both sides (shared with the sibling region _simple_assertion)

the three .add((s, p, o)) calls become three one-line g{...} islands; prefixes declared for the three vocabularies actually used: hycl: (nanopub.namespaces.HYCL), prov: and dc:. The draft's rdf:, dcterms: and xsd: declarations were dropped, none is used

NEGATIVE FINDING (same as the sibling NanopubClaim.__init__): Nanopub.assertion / .provenance / .pubinfo are READ-ONLY properties, and ldpy's only graph-mutation idiom is the augmented assignment 'G += g{...}', which needs an assignable target -- 'np.assertion += g{...}' raises AttributeError: property has no setter. The translation therefore has to spell the operator out as np.assertion.__iadd__(g{...}), which is clearly less natural than the original .add(); a non-assigning form is missing from the notation
runtime-computed terms stay Python and are interpolated: {np.assertion.identifier} and {np._metadata.namespace[""]} (a nested double-quoted string inside an island interpolation transpiles fine)
Literal("test claim") / Literal("tester") become bare "test claim" / "tester" inside the islands (node() coerces a str to the identical plain Literal)
the mechanical draft had inserted the @prefix block in the middle of the parenthesised 'from nanopub import (' list, which is not valid ldpy; the declarations now follow all imports

demo harness added identically to both sides: the region returns a Nanopub, which the harness cannot compare, so the demo calls it twice -- once with the default conf (covering the 'conf is None' branch) and once with a NanopubConf disabling add_prov/pubinfo_generated_time -- and exposes the resulting named graphs plus the printed is_valid verdicts. The pubinfo graph of the default call is NOT compared: the Nanopub constructor stamps it with a wall-clock prov:generatedAtTime that no two runs can share (an rdflib/nanopub non-determinism, unrelated to the notation)
